messages:
Anita: Heads-up — we've got a small but noisy issue: a handful of tenants saw silent version switches when `X-API-Version` was missing. Repro and quick dump below, want opinions on fallback policy and console affordances.

Jia: Which tenants? proxy vs client libs?

Anita: Two tenants via Fastly-ish CDN, one direct SDK. Logs show the header was stripped for edge requests. Fallback routed to default `v2` variant and their workload cost jumped.

Sam: Confirmed in proxy logs. Example curl that fails to preserve header:
```
curl -H 'X-API-Version: v1' https://api.redwood.ai/generate
```
Edge strip means service never sees it -> routing chooses default.

Manny: OOF. Current fallback is `DEFAULT_ORDER = [v2, v1]`. That feels risky. Suggest we add `LAST_SEEN` fallback: prefer the last successful route for that token/tenant if header absent.

Clare: Agree on `LAST_SEEN`. Also we need telemetry: count of requests with header-missing + route chosen + per-tenant delta in token cost. Right now it's invisible in billing dashboards.

Jia: I'll add a sampling probe to trace header-missing -> route. Proposal: 0.1% full payloads, 100% meta events (route-chosen, headers-present). Chart: "header_absent_route_breakdown".

Anita: Nice. UX question: do we show a console warning/banner for tenants with >1% header-missing or >2x cost delta in 24h? Or we auto-pin their tenant to `LAST_SEEN` for 48hrs and show a banner with opt-out.

Sam: Auto-pin is convenient but risky (makes rollback/rollforward harder). Maybe auto-suggest pin (banner + single-click confirm) instead of auto-enforce.

Manny: Implementation note: `LAST_SEEN` needs a TTL and GDPR-safe keying (token hash). Should be cheap — store last route id per token in routing cache with TTL 7d.

Clare: Also add events to billing pipeline: when route changes for a token, emit `route_switch` event with before/after model id so we can attribute cost spikes.

deploy-bot: Routing change branch (last-seen fallback) is currently in canary @ 5% traffic in us-west. Rollout ETA: 2h.

Anita: If canary is live, let's hold banners until we have the metric. Jia, hook your probe to the canary traffic and report.

Jia: On it. I'll post a Grafana link when done. Query will include `tenant_id`, `token_hash`, `route_before`, `route_after`, `header_present`.

Sam: One more: what about tenants that use long-running streaming sessions — pining mid-stream could be weird. Need to ensure `LAST_SEEN` only affects new requests, not active connections.

Manny: Yep — routing decisions occur at request start. We'll document it: "pinning affects new connections only".

Clare: Copy for console banner draft:
"We detected requests where version headers were removed by an intermediary. We recommend enabling 'preserve routing' to keep your current model version for new requests. Learn more [link]"

Anita: Action items:
- Jia: sampling probe + canary dashboard (ETA 6h)
- Sam: PR to add `LAST_SEEN` fallback with TTL and unit tests (ETA EOD)
- Manny: routing cache changes + docs (ETA 2d)
- Clare: billing event + dashboard tile (ETA 1d)
- Anita: banner copy + help center article (ETA 1d)

Jia: ACK. Will ping when graphs up :eyes:

Sam: Opening the PR now and linking canary URL here.

Anita: Thanks team. If we see anything weird in the canary we'll pause the rollout. No objections, I'll mark this as the preferred fallback pattern for the console UX review on Friday.

Manny: :thumbsup:

Clare: :rocket:

incident-bot: New alert rule created: header_absent_rate > 1% for any tenant -> page on-call.

Anita: Good catch. Thanks everyone — follow-ups in #eng-platform/infra sync on Friday.
